senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; preced.) flavor, scent, odor; sense of smell.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 43b:3">Ber. 43ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 150:6">Ps. CL, 6</cite>) <he>איזהו דבר … זה הר׳</he> what is the thing which the soul enjoys and from which the body has no material benefit? It is smell.

<cite ref="Psalms 150:6">Ib.</cite> <he>עתידים … שיתנו ר׳ וכ׳</he> in the future the young men of Israel shall give forth sweet savor (of purity) like the Lebanon (ref. to <cite ref="Hosea 14:7">Hos. XIV, 7</cite>).
Lev. R. s. 30; a. v. fr.—Trnsf. (cmp. אָבָק) slight resemblance, a suspicion of.

<cite ref="Gittin 86b:18-19">Gitt. 86ᵇ</cite> <he>אף ר׳ הגט אין בו</he> it has not even the slightest resemblance to a letter of divorce (by which the woman concerned might be precluded from marrying a priest); Y. ib. IX, 50ᵇ top <he>אפי׳ ר׳ פסול אין בה</he> there is not a suspicion of disqualification in her case.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 1:2:10">Y. Sot. I, 16ᵈ</cite> top <he>מר׳ ערוה נגעו בה</he> something of the odor of incest has touched her (the rival wife of a faithless woman); a. e.—Pl. <he>ריחוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:3:1">Cant. R. to I, 3</cite> <he>כל … ר׳ היו וכ׳</he> all the songs which the ancients recited before thee were merely sweet savors, but we (say), ‘oil that is poured forth is thy name’; <he>כל המצות … ר׳ היו וכ׳</he> all the pious deeds … were merely flavors, but &c.; a. e.
